## What a user of the old system will notice

**Nothing, on the happy path.** Every response shape, status code, and the two documented
historical quirks (200-empty-object on a missing ticket, int-or-string `priority`) are frozen
(PB-005). The UI (`svc-ui`) should work against the new backend without a single line of its
own code changing.

**Ticket closing stops going down when email is slow.** The one thing PB-001 exists to fix:
closing a ticket (and requesting a password reset) no longer waits on an SMTP round-trip.
Today, an SMTP outage doesn't just slow these two requests — the ticket-close database update
already commits before the email is attempted, so a slow/failed SMTP call today reports a
false 500 for a ticket that actually did close. After WO-002/WO-004 land, the response is
prompt and honest regardless of mail-transport health.

**Password reset links still work exactly the same way from the outside** — request an email,
get a token, confirm within 30 minutes, invalid and expired tokens still look identical (no
information leakage). What changes is invisible to the user: the token is no longer a
predictable MD5 hash sitting in a bare, unindexed table (PB-002).

**New tickets can no longer silently collide on the same slug** — once WO-005 ships (currently
blocked on a human ruling, OQ-001, about exactly *how* a collision should be handled: reject,
auto-suffix, or include the ticket id in every slug).

## What a user of the old system will NOT get (explicitly out of scope)

No new features. No UI changes. No password-changing functionality (there isn't any today
either — see `glossary.md`'s note on that). If OQ-002 rules that the app needs its own
authentication, that would be the one exception — but it's a ruling this workspace flags as
unresolved, not a change already decided.
